- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.00) or shows sudden reversal (e.g., -1.00), model often overpredicts downward trend; reduce forecast slope or add early reversal buffer.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the first 5–7 days of a new trend (especially after sentiment shift), so apply a “lag correction” by +2–5% for the first 5–7 forecast days.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows mean-reversion pattern (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true mean (especially after 10+ days of negative sentiment), so add 1–3% upward bias to mean forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
